newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Rashid Hussain, Maybank seen set on deal price.
newsitem.headline: Rashid Hussain, Maybank seen set on deal price.

text.p: After drawn-out talks, Rashid Hussain Bhd and Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) are believed to have settled on a price of 8.75 ringgit ($3.50) to 8.85 ringgit a share for Maybank's stake in Kwong Yik Bank Bhd, analysts said.
Shares of all three have been suspended since October 21 and stockbrokerage Rashid said on October 25 that it was in talks to buy Malaysia's largest bank, Maybank's 75 percent stake in Kwong Yik.
In addition, the stock of DCB Holdings Bhd, Rashid's 20-percent owned associate banking unit, had also been suspended.
On Tuesday, the four stocks' suspensions were extended by 10 trading days to December 3 to allow the companies to complete their deal. Analysts said a deal could be announced as early as next week.

Banking analyst Desmond Ch'ng at South Johor Securities said on Friday that the price for Kwong Yik was believed to be between 8.80 ringgit and 8.85 ringgit a share or over two billion ringgit for the entire stake.

He estimated the fair value of Kwong Yik at between 7.80-8.20 ringgit a share, but added the bank may deserve a premium price because the deal with Rashid is for a controlling stake, unlike other recent bank deals.

"My guess is that it's probably 8.75 to maybe 8.80 ringgit," said an institutional dealer at a local brokerage firm. "What we heard was there was still a gap between Maybank and Rashid (prices) but that the gap is narrowing."
Maybank was speculated to have been asking between nine ringgit and 10 ringgit a share for Kwong Yik, while Rashid was said to be pushing to pay seven ringgit a share.
A spokesman at Rashid Hussain, which operates Malaysia's largest institutional stockbroker and also develops property, declined comment on the speculation as did a spokeswoman at Maybank.
Analysts expect Rashid to inject Kwong Yik into DCB Holdings, the parent of DCB Bank Bhd, creating Malaysia's third largest bank as measured by assets.
What Maybank would gain from the deal, besides a large sum of cash, is adherence to a Malaysian banking requirement that disallows a bank from holding two banking licenses, they said.

At least one piece of the Rashid-Kwong Yik deal seemed to fall in place this week, after diversified Malaysian Resources Corp Bhd (MRCB) announced on Wednesday that it had agreed to buy 19.05 percent of Rashid Hussain for 1.04 billion ringgit in MRCB stock.

Together with shares already purchased in the open market, MRCB said it has a total stake of 20.06 percent of Rashid. The deal gives MRCB, already in media and communications as well as power generation, exposure to financial services.
